Subject: Re: Production degradation — sustained latency + 5xx spike (EverWell prod)

Tracking notes from the triage call: 
- Symptom: sudden P95 jump and 5xx bursts coincident with a high prefix-cache miss rate for the identity model.
- Initial root cause hypothesis: KV cache eviction storm triggered by a background bulk-refresh job that ramped at 08:40 ET; this caused cache thrash and forced more long-path inference runs.
- Immediate mitigations applied (09:30 ET):
  * disabled the scheduled bulk-refresh for EverWell tenant (rolled back job config).
  * activated a targeted caching layer pin for hot prefixes for EverWell.
  * temporarily bumped autoscaler min replicas by 25% for the EverWell Dedicated pool.
- Observed effect (09:33–09:40 ET): 5xx rate reduced from 18% -> 4.2%; P95 trending down to ~390ms.

Next steps:
- Deploy a lightweight canary variant (quantized) to absorb bursty long-path requests (ETA 10:00 ET).
- Post-mitigation validation window 10:00–10:20 ET; plan to provide consolidated metrics.

Attachment: latency-sla-metrics-20270618.csv (updated with post-mitigation slice).

-David

Director, Site Reliability Engineering

Subject: EverWell — status update and next steps (post incident containment)

Good evening all — quick consolidated summary following containment actions and the executive check-in.

1) What we observed: transient KV cache eviction storm caused cache thrash; secondary effect increased inference long-paths and autoscaler lag which produced elevated P95 and 5xx for ~30 minutes.
2) Actions taken: disabled offending refresh job; applied targeted cache pins; increased dedicated replica floor; deployed quantized canary variant.
3) Outcome: end-user impact reduced immediately; P95 stabilized ~280–350ms and 5xx settled under 1% by 11:15 ET.
4) Customer commitments from Redwood:
   - Incident report and timeline within 48 hours (we will include root cause, mitigation, and concrete fixes).
   - Proposal for a one-time goodwill credit; Rishi will follow up with a draft (attached: proposed-compensation-draft-v2.docx).
   - Operational fixes: automatic bulk-refresh safety guard, improved eviction thresholds, and an alert to detect cache-storm patterns.

Next steps / owners:
- Rishi: finalize compensation draft and legal/finance loop (ETA 24–36 hrs).
- David + SRE: deliver patched safety guard and canary test in staging (ETA 72 hrs).
- Marissa/Kim: post-incident customer comm and FAQ (ETA 24 hrs).
- Laura: schedule an executive postmortem (invite to follow) and coordinate board-level summary if required.

If EverWell would like an early read of the incident report, we can share a draft tomorrow morning. Thank you for your partnership and patience while we stabilized this.

—Laura
